chunks: ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked him about the blood-money for intentional killing, where a man kills another man deliberately. He said: He said, “One hundred of the mature male camels; and if there are no camels, then in place of each camel there are twenty of the male sheep.”

key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the primary unit of compensation in this ruling
key_terms.الْعَمْدِ: intentionality; deliberate commission of the act
key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: sheep, used here as a substitute valuation when camels are unavailable
key_terms.دِيَةِ: blood-money; the legally mandated compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.فُحُولَةِ: male livestock, specifically males used in assessing compensation here

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for intentional killing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for the diyah of intentional homicide. It specifies that the compensation is one hundred mature male camels, and if camels are unavailable, each camel is replaced by twenty male sheep. The narration is part of discussions on judicial rulings, blood-money, and the administration of justice in Islamic law.
